source.title: Geneshift: Impact of different scenario shift on Jailbreaking LLM
source.authors: Tian-Yi Wu; Zhiwei Xue; Yue Liu; Jia-Heng Zhang; Bryan Hooi; S. Ng

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops a scenario-shift jailbreak attack and reports how that method performs. It does not test the claim's fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant-prefill, suffix/decoding, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-response success rates for its scenario-shift attack, its ablation, and its own method's benchmark results. Those outcomes are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version: the tested intervention is scenario shifting, not the specific interventions named by V1–V7. Results for other methods in Table 1 and the transfer results in Table 5 are not included. Table 2 does not state which of the two evaluation metrics its rates use.
record.test_reason: This is a jailbreak-method paper. GeneShift uses genetic search over scenario-shift prompt transformations, and the paper reports only that attack's success on GPT-4o mini, with transfer to GPT-4o. It does not measure fine-tuning effects (V1, V2), per-token KL (V3), prefill, suffix or decoding attacks as its own intervention (V4), parameter localization (V5), causes of shallowness (V6) or deepening (V7). It does not rely on the shallow-alignment finding as a tool. Qi et al. 2023, an original source, is cited only as a reference for the GPT-based judge. The findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that GeneShift, a black-box attack using genetic search over scenario shifts, elicits detailed harmful content while keeping a benign facade. They report that it outperforms white-box and black-box baselines on both ASR-DICT and ASR-GPT on GPT-4o mini, raising ASR-GPT from 0% to 60%, and that its prompts transfer to GPT-4o. They warn that stronger defenses are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates black-box scenario-shift prompting and a genetic-algorithm attack, not the original fine-tuning or token-depth methods. It uses prompt-based attack success rates.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported success varies across scenario-shift types and harmful-request categories (Table 2); adding scenario-shift context and then genetic-algorithm optimization changes the ablation results (Table 3).

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-4o mini, direct harmful queries reach 0.00% ASR-GPT. Adding scenario-shift context raises this to 18.00%, and genetic search over shifts raises it to 60.00% (Table 3). Per-shift success varies by request type from 0% to 30.30% (Table 2). GeneShift prompts transfer to GPT-4o at 53.08% ASR-GPT (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Black-box scenario-shift prompting, optimized by genetic search, bypasses refusal in closed safety-trained models, with effectiveness depending on how well the shift matches the request type.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says it will open-source code but gives no URL.
record.peer_reviewed: Published at ICLR 2025 Workshop on Foundation Models in the Wild.
record.problems: Main experiments are reported on GPT-4o mini; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Table 2 does not identify whether its success rates are ASR-DICT or ASR-GPT. The paper also describes the attack as single-turn in the method section but calls it multi-turn in the appendix.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 has 20 other scenario-shift/request-type cells not extracted because of the 60-row cap and priority was given to the five request-type columns retained. Table 5 transfer results and other-method benchmark rows from Table 1 were left out; the listed versions are not tested. Table 2 cells retained: all ten scenario shifts for Illegal Activity, Physical Harm, Economic Harm, Privacy Violence, and Fraud.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and the resulting compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models by response position.
Prefilling, suffixes and decoding changes as the tested intervention. Scenario-shift prompting is a different input-side attack; GCG appears only as a comparison baseline.
Localization of safety in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether the data or training objective causes the shallowness.
Deepening interventions and how robust they are.

record.verdict_notes: Recommend changing the relation from uses_without_test/T4 to cites_only/T6, since shallow alignment is not used as a tool. Table 1 does report a GCG suffix baseline on GPT-4o mini at 3.46% ASR-DICT and 2.50% ASR-GPT. This is low suffix-attack success on a closed model, tangentially relevant to V4, but it is a comparison baseline with no stated transfer setup, so it is not treated as a test. Table 2's 20 Malware and Hate Speech cells are declared left out. Only one model is evaluated, with no uncertainty reported. The method section calls the attack single-turn, while the appendix calls it multi-turn.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning, number of fine-tuning examples, and resulting refusal/compliance.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling a compliant opening, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes; the paper tests scenario-shift prompts instead.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
Training intended to spread safety beyond the first tokens and its robustness.
